findings.text: the done-when requires every test file importing a changed module to pass with zero added failures against the base, but the run's own after_suite records exit_status 1 with 100 passed and 1 failed - tests/test_frozen_current_flux_image_gate.py::test_render_only_reproduces_receipted_panel_set. The failure is genuinely introduced by the change (it passes at base, fails at head; reproduced both ways) and is the intended consequence of masking the gate-b contour (the committed panels were drawn by the pre-mask tricontour; the only remedy is regenerating those committed panels, which the same brief forbids this node to do. The node discloses it honestly, attributes it to the exact commit, and names the remediation and the out-of-scope reason; it is a real added failure and belongs on the follow-on list rather than triaged here.

the five repaired sites are pinned by no automated assertion. The scanner's test file scans benchmarks/ and docs/figures/ but asserts only membership of control sites in other files (its own docstring says it asserts no total count), so a future edit that removes a wall= argument from any of the three repaired drivers would not redden the suite. Only a manual run of tests/renderer_wall_scan.py would catch such a regression.

gate_arms_note: The reviewed run records real suite arms. baseline_suite (revision 68762d3639, exit 0, 101 passed) was run as a scratch-tree swap: the three drivers were restored to base content in the head worktree, declared through measurement_module/measurement_cwd; after_suite (revision 972444a33, exit 1, 100 passed 1 failed) ran at the committed head on a clean tree. Its own gate arms are the scanner logs logs/base-scanner.log (five sites, EXIT=1) and logs/head-scanner.log (none, EXIT=0), plus logs/guard-fires.log. I reproduced the scanner over my worktree at base content (five sites, EXIT=1; logs/review-scan-base.log) and over the reviewed worktree at head 972444a3 (none, EXIT=0; logs/review-scan-head.log), the guard-fires probe exactly (logs/review-guard-fires.log), and the single failing test at both arms (base passes, head fails). after - base failure set difference = {that one id}, so added_failure_count = 1. The id is named in full in the run's manifest follow_ons, so the read-time added-failure derivation retires it by name and the stored total is not capped.

item_verdicts.diff: three files, 28 insertions and 12 deletions; every added wall argument is in scope at its call site and each edit is the minimal mask change.
item_verdicts.done_when: the scanner gate exits 0 at head and 1 at base as required, but the same done-when's 'zero added failures' clause is unmet - the after_suite adds one failure.
item_verdicts.goal: read the goal and the five-site scanner measure; all five unguarded calls are routed through the wall mask and the scanner reproduces five sites at base and none at head.
item_verdicts.manifest: manifest carries a landing line, both suite arms as JSON, the scanner arms, the guard-fires result and a precise follow-on; base_log_revision/head_log_revision read absent because the log headers spell the revision differently.

justifications.durability: The fix is real and pinned by a falsifiable source scan whose two arms I reproduced (five sites -> none) and by a guard-fires probe that shows the mask actually removes out-of-wall vertices. Three weaknesses. (1) The node's own suite is red at the landing revision: after_suite exits 1 with one added failure, tests/test_frozen_current_flux_image_gate.py::test_render_only_reproduces_receipted_panel_set, which compares a fresh render against the committed gate-b panels and can only be re-greened by regenerating those panels - work the same brief forbids this node to do. So the landing leaves a failing test in the suite, resolved only by the separately dispatched regeneration wave the node names. (2) The five repaired sites are pinned by no automated assertion: tests/renderer_wall_scan.py scans benchmarks/ and docs/figures/ but its expectations are membership tests on control sites in other files, so removing a wall= argument from any of the three repaired drivers would not redden any test. (3) The base arm is a scratch-tree swap rather than a checked-out base revision; it is declared and adequate, but it is not a clean-room base arm.
justifications.evidence: Every headline reproduces first-hand. Scanner gate: base 68762d36 -> five named sites, EXIT=1; head 972444a3 -> none, EXIT=0 (both rerun by me, logs on disk). The negative control is real: it is the base arm of the same command and it lists exactly the five sites the fix names, matching the manifest's evidence_inputs line-for-line. The guard-fires probe reproduces exactly (168/830 and 29/126 outside unguarded; 0 outside guarded; logs/review-guard-fires.log). Both suite arms are logged with a header naming revision, tree and command: baseline_suite 68762d36 exits 0 with 101 passed (a scratch-tree swap of the three drivers to base content, declared via measurement_module/measurement_cwd), after_suite 972444a3 exits 1 with 100 passed and 1 failed. I confirmed the added failure is caused by the change, not pre-existing: tests/test_frozen_current_flux_image_gate.py::test_render_only_reproduces_receipted_panel_set passes at base (my worktree, logs/review-failing-test-base.log, 1 passed in 30.51s) and fails at head (reviewed worktree, logs/review-failing-test-head.log, 1 failed in 21.72s). Deductions: (1) the done-when requires 'zero added failures against the base' and the run added one; the run reports this honestly rather than claiming otherwise, but the clause is unmet. (2) The manifest's base_log_revision/head_log_revision read absent because the suite-log headers spell the revision 'rev <sha>' rather than 'revision <sha>', so a reader cannot tie the count to a commit from the header alone.
justifications.fit: Minimal and idiomatic. Five call sites each gain the wall argument the driver already holds, and the two frozen-gate tricontour calls move to the existing nova.media.poloidal.draw_scattered_contours helper rather than hand-masking - the right reuse, since that helper owns the triangle-outside-wall masking and keeps the level array as data. No new helper, no new dependency, no signature change to the painters. Both wall spellings in use are accepted by coerce_wall_units (a WallUnit collection at diverted:200 and a (wall,) tuple at solve_gate:1541,1544), and level arrays stay shared/explicit. No plan/sprint/ticket identifier appears in names or comments. Minor: reordering wall_units=(wall,) above the two draw_flux_contours calls is a small readability win but slightly widens the diff.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The goal - route every unguarded scattered-field renderer call in this batch through the wall mask - is fully met and independently reproduced. I reran the scanner tests/renderer_wall_scan.py over the three drivers: at the base content (my worktree, base revision 68762d36) it printed exactly the five sites (diverted_chord_response_attribution.py:200 draw_flux_contours; solve_program_size_gate.py:1541,1544 draw_flux_contours; frozen_current_flux_image_gate.py:1144,1208 tricontour) and exited 1, and at the reviewed head 972444a3 the same command printed nothing and exited 0 (logs/review-scan-base.log, logs/review-scan-head.log). I read all three edits in the commit diff and every added wall argument is genuinely in scope at its call site: diverted_chord_response_attribution.py:200 passes wall=units, the WallUnit collection the driver already draws; solve_program_size_gate.py:1541,1544 pass wall=wall_units with wall_units=(wall,) moved above both calls; and the two frozen-gate tricontour calls move to nova.media.poloidal.draw_scattered_contours with the wall the driver holds, keeping the filled-level floor as data via np.maximum(absolute, error_levels[0]). The guard demonstrably fires: against a concave C vessel, unguarded draw_flux_contours put 168 of 830 contour vertices outside the wall and a raw tricontour put 29 of 126 outside, while both guarded routes put 0 outside (I reran the probe, logs/review-guard-fires.log). Not full marks only because the done-when's separate 'zero added failures' clause is unmet, which is an evidence/durability matter rather than a failure of the masking goal.
justifications.scope_discipline: The review range 68762d36..972444a3 touches exactly the three granted benchmark drivers; the report lands at the granted reports path and no figure directory is written. No source under nova/ is edited, no plan file, no shared index and no concurrent-node path is touched. The single commit 972444a3 carries a conventional subject and an explanatory body stating what changed and why (five calls drew interpolated field unmasked; the wall the driver already holds is passed; scanner reports five at base and none after), and it carries no AI-attribution trailer. A scan of the added lines finds no plan/stage/ticket/version label and no _v2/_new/_final suffix. The node also respects its 'do not re-render committed figures' instruction: no figure was regenerated, and the committed figure set is unchanged.
